messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Apr 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Sponsor snapshot — business outcomes, procurement constraints, escalation items

Thanks for your time today — quick written recap so we have a single source of truth. Notes below are from our call with Samantha (CTO) and Carlos (Head of ML Ops). Please flag anything I missed.

TL;DR
- BlueHorizon priority: reduce inference cost and stabilize tail latency for patient-facing features while meeting EU data residency and audit requirements.
- Procurement path: vendor security review (SOC2 attestation + evidence), legal IP/indemnity negotiation, PO/term sheet in 6-12 weeks depending on procurement load.
- Next immediate step: Redwood provides SOC2 evidence pack + architecture whitepaper; BlueHorizon to share procurement POC and vendor evaluation checklist by 2026-04-08.

Pain points we captured
- Latency spikes at high concurrency: 95th->99th latency increases cause visible UI slowdowns during batch ingest windows.
- Unit cost volatility: current per-token costs make ML features uneconomical for broader rollout.
- Compliance: EU data residency + strict audit trail requirements for PHI-adjacent metadata.

Business outcomes BlueHorizon wants
- Reduce per-inference unit cost by ~40% to enable productization across three teams (Patient Messaging, Intake, Insights).
- 99th percentile latency < 300ms for 2k concurrent sessions in primary region.
- Private deployment option for EU region with KMS integration and 12-month audit logs.

Procurement constraints & timeline
- Must pass security questionnaire and provide SOC2 report: procurement will kick off vendor comparisons once security pack is received (target window 1 week).
- Legal has standard clauses around IP and data processing; Carlos said minor redlines expected but indemnity language may take longer.
- Budget cadence: headcount vs license model — decision expected during Q3 budget cycle; pilot spend pre-approved up to an internal threshold subject to Marissa/Finance sign-off.

Risks / escalation items
- Data residency: need clear architecture for EU private deployment and proof of audit logs retention.
- Performance: kernel-level optimizations may be required to hit 99th percentile SLA — will need an early engineering validation step.
- Contracting cadence: Legal + Procurement parallel path to avoid serial blockers.

Agreed next steps (owners / dates)
1) Redwood: Send SOC2 evidence pack + architecture whitepaper (Diego) — by 2026-04-06 — attachment: bluehorizon-redlines-v1.pdf (redlines + initial SOW stub).
2) BlueHorizon: Share procurement checklist + procurement POC contact (Carlos) — by 2026-04-08.
3) Redwood/Product: Run short perf validation on representative workload and share results (Karthik + Eng) — internal target 2026-04-12.
4) Redwood/Sales Ops: Prepare pilot commercial proposal including a modest pilot credit and dedicated capacity options (Marissa) — draft by 2026-04-09.

Attachments referenced: bluehorizon-redlines-v1.pdf (initial SOW + redline), procurement-matrix.xlsx (sample procurement mapping).

If that aligns, I'll post the SOC2 link and open the HubSpot deal record with the items above. Thanks again — excited to move this forward.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
